problem:
Which of the following are elementary matrices?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ 3 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following are elementary matrices?

$$
Q=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 7\end{aligned}],\,E=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
An elementary matrix is a matrix obtained from the identity matrix by applying exactly one elementary row operation. 

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- The matrix $Q$ is an elementary matrix because it can be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}:=3{R}_{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{2}:=3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =Q\end{aligned}
$$

- The matrix $W$ is not an elementary matrix because it can't be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying only one elementary row operation.

- The matrix $E$ is an elementary matrix because it can be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-4){R}_{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-4){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, only $Q$ and $E$ are elementary matrices.
